subject: NeuralByte Dedicated Sizing — Commitment Pathway Questionnaire
messages:
From: Ari Kaplan <ari@neuralbyte.ai>
To: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Dedicated capacity sizing intake (NeuralByte)

Hi Dylan,

Thanks for the quick intro last week. Attached is a short traffic snapshot (CSV) pulled from our staging telemetry that shows daily tokens, average prompt/response lengths, and session counts for the last 30 days. We're starting a pilot that will move to paid reserved capacity if the numbers and pricing look reasonable.

High-level context: we expect 10k daily active sessions initially with a 5% weekly growth ramp for three months. Typical call pattern is chat-style multi-turn sessions (avg 4 turns), and we care about 95th percentile latency under 350ms for single-turn inference.

Can you share a short questionnaire or checklist we can fill out that captures the data you'll need to size a dedicated fleet (concurrency, token mix, burst profile, model tolerance, etc.)? Also happy to set a short call early next week.

Attachments: neuralbyte_traffic_snapshot.csv (csv)

Thanks,
Ari Kaplan
Head of Platform
NeuralByte
ari@neuralbyte.ai

From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@neuralbyte.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-22T16:10:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing intake (NeuralByte)

Thanks Ari — got the snapshot and good context. I'm looping in Marissa (solutions) and Karthik (fleet planning) so we can produce a concise sizing recommendation. Below is a short questionnaire we request for pre-sales sizing; if you can paste answers inline or attach a filled sheet that works. I've also proposed a 30-min slot (link below) to walk through any clarifications.

Required sizing inputs (short form):
1) Expected sustained QPS and peak burst QPS (tokens/sec or requests/sec). If you have per-minute buckets, attach a sample.
2) Concurrency per-session vs. concurrency per-tenant (do you expect many parallel sessions from the same user or across users?).
3) Prompt length distribution (tokens): min/median/p95/max.
4) Response length distribution (tokens): min/median/p95/max.
5) Average turns per session and whether sessions keep KV cache across turns.
6) Latency SLOs (p50/p95/p99) and maximum allowable cold-start/queueing time.
7) Acceptable model family and lowest acceptable quantization (FP16, int8/4bit) — e.g., can you accept 4-bit quantized variants for cost savings?
8) Throughput tolerance for batching (max added latency allowed for batching in exchange for cost).
9) Any hard data residency / network egress constraints (region, VPC, on-prem).
10) Business timeline & PO/contract lead time (when do you plan to commit).

Optional helpful artifacts: (a) representative prompt+response pairs (anonymized), (b) hourly/daily burst traces, (c) percentage of requests that are stateless vs. stateful.

Proposed next step: 30-min walkthrough. Schedule: https://calendar.google.com/event?eid=xyz123call
I'll attach a one-page mutual action plan draft after the call for sign-off.

Attachments (sent internally): dedicated_sizing_questionnaire.xlsx (we will attach the file in a follow-up)

Best,
Dylan Brooks
Senior Solutions Architect, Redwood Inference

From: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@neuralbyte.ai>
Cc: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-23T09:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing intake (NeuralByte)

Hi Ari — quick technical follow-ups to help us avoid back-and-forth during sizing:

- Model family: which model(s) are you currently running in staging? (e.g., Llama2-70B, or an instruction-tuned 30B). If you're evaluating multiple, rank them by priority.
- KV cache usage: do sessions rely on long KV caches retained across turns (e.g., >2k tokens)? That affects memory footprint per session.
- Batching behavior: do you have strict single-request latency ceilings, or can you accept an additional 25–50ms for batching to improve GPU utilization?
- Retry/backoff pattern: are clients aggressive with retries on 429/5xx or do they have exponential backoff?
- Tokenization: are prompts pre-tokenized at the client or do you send raw text? If pre-tokenized, include tokenizer (BPE/cl100k).
- Growth projection: you mentioned 5% weekly for 3 months — can you confirm whether that is linear or cohort-driven burst growth (spikey).

From the CSV I pulled a quick sketch: median prompt ~45 tokens, median response ~210 tokens, p95 response ~980 tokens (yikes — long tails matter). Please attach a small sample of ~20 anonymized prompt/response pairs so we can validate p95 behavior.

I've attached a short PDF with token distribution guidance (neuralbyte_token_distribution.pdf) and a lightweight notes file with how we map token mix to GPU SKU choices. We'll include a filled questionnaire (xlsx) in the follow-up when we get your inputs.

Attachments: neuralbyte_token_distribution.pdf (pdf)

Thanks,
Marissa Cole
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Dylan Brooks <dylan@redwoodinference.com>
To: Ari Kaplan <ari@neuralbyte.ai>, NeuralByte Procurement <procurement@neuralbyte.ai>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa@redwoodinference.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik@redwoodinference.com>
Date: 2028-07-25T11:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Dedicated capacity sizing intake (NeuralByte)

Ari — thanks for the quick turn. Marissa's notes are spot on. Next steps from our side:

1) Please fill the short questionnaire Dylan sent (or attach the filled xlsx). If you can paste p95/p99 numbers for response lengths that will materially change the sizing.
2) Share 15–20 anonymized prompt/response pairs (we will not store PII).
3) We'll produce a sizing recommendation within 48 hours of receiving the questionnaire and samples. Expect: GPU SKU mix, estimated reserved slots, expected p95 latency at baseline and under 3x burst, and cost estimate with two commitment tiers.

We've attached a one-page mutual action plan draft for the pilot -> reserved commitment pathway (mutual_action_plan_draft.docx). Can Procurement confirm an internal PO timeline (standard 30–45 days?) so we can line up capacity and preferred SKUs?
